comment: Gate slice (issue 02) re-measure: coredoc-spec is 25,621 B after the standalone-acceptance commands and the artifact-path handoff, so its ceiling moves from 25,600 to 26,624 B; coredoc-workflows is 12,536 B after the stage-gate, skip-flag and parked-run rules, so its ceiling moves from 11,264 to 13,312 B. Both keep more than 512 B of headroom for issue 04's description sentence. Earlier OSS backport measurement: 5,809 catalog bytes across 23 skills after adding optional Jira and Git delivery. Router growth wires those capabilities and branch-start; implementation growth preserves existing intent guidance while adding branch-start. Body ceilings keep at least 512 B of headroom; these are bytes, not token estimates. Re-measure and justify increases; do not regenerate ceilings automatically. Issue 04 (gate sentences) re-measure: appending the mandated gate sentence to four descriptions moves coredoc-review to 344 B, coredoc-spec to 463 B, coredoc-implement to 503 B and coredoc-workflows to 547 B of catalog, and the catalog total from 5,809 to 6,613 B. The sentences are fixed wording and the pre-existing halves are all trigger phrases (the routed intents, the change kinds, the review surfaces), so nothing could be trimmed without losing a trigger: perSkillCatalogMaxBytes moves from 350 to 560 B and catalogMaxBytes from 6,100 to 6,700 B, leaving 13 B of per-skill and 87 B of catalog headroom. Body ceilings are unchanged and still hold (spec 25,863/26,624; workflows 12,945/13,312; implement 10,015/11,264; review 15,751/17,408). 2026-09-17: coredoc-spec's description no longer carries the gate sentence (it suppressed triggering: 0/9 fires on explicit spec prompts with it, 12/18 overall without), so the issue-04 four-description figures now describe three; every ceiling is unchanged. 2026-09-17, coredoc-prd: the new skill's body is 15.8 KB (ceiling 16,384) and its 444 B catalog entry moves the total from 6,613 to 7,043 B, so catalogMaxBytes is the measured 7,043 plus 512 B, 7,555. The same commit builds the 2,489 B PRD↔spec contract partial into coredoc-spec, which had 11 B of headroom after two rounds of prose cuts; its body is 29,151 B, so its ceiling moves from 26,624 to 29,696 B, the smallest 1,024 multiple keeping 512 B of headroom. 2026-09-17, revision 2: coredoc-prd gains proportionality rules and the closing brief (body 16.7 KB), so its ceiling moves from 16,384 to 17,408 B; coredoc-spec's lifecycle mechanics moved to resources/methodology/spec-lifecycle.md but the three input modes, sizing and PRD shape it gained weigh more than they removed, so its body stays near 29.1 KB and its 29,696 B ceiling is unchanged rather than restored to 26,624. 2026-09-22 feedback remediation: extracted detailed evidence rules into an on-demand method to avoid multiplying them into every skill. Remaining measured bodies are investigate 13,401 B, PRD 17,861 B and spec 30,604 B; the additions cover asynchronous independent question rounds, closure and reuse. Their ceilings move to 14,336 / 18,432 / 31,744 B, preserving at least 512 B headroom. Other ceilings are unchanged. 2026-09-22 continuation: two focused skills add 370 description bytes (design 1445 B, verify 1466 B total); each gets a 2048 B body ceiling. Router is 13769 B after explicit specialization and reuse entrypoints, so its ceiling becomes 14336 B. Existing other ceilings remain unchanged.
